question: How can we change the margins of a document in MS Word?
solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Margins in MS Word can be adjusted using the **Layout tab**, where the **Margins option** is located.
 
• The Layout tab provides predefined margin settings such as **Normal, Narrow, Moderate, Wide, Mirrored**, and allows **custom margin adjustments**.
 
• To modify margins, navigate to Layout tab -> Margins -> Choose a predefined option or select "Custom Margins" for advanced adjustments.
 
• Custom margins can be set by defining the **Top, Bottom, Left, and Right** margins in the Page Setup dialog box.
 
• Changing margins affects the **entire document** or can be limited to specific sections using section breaks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Page Setup:**

 
 
• The Page Setup dialog box contains options to modify margins, paper size, orientation, and layout settings.
 
• It can be accessed through the Layout tab or by right-clicking on the ruler.
 
 
 
• **Section Breaks:**
 
 
• Section breaks allow users to create different margin setups within a single document.
 
• They can be added via Layout tab -> Breaks -> Select Section Break type.
 
 
 
• **Ruler Adjustment:**
 
 
• Margins can also be adjusted using the ruler by dragging the margin indicators directly.
 
• This method offers a quick way to visually adjust margins without using the Layout tab.
 
 
 
• **Orientation Impact:**
 
 
• Changing page orientation (Portrait or Landscape) can influence margin settings.
 
• Orientation settings are available in the Layout tab -> Orientation.
